title: No-back-dating derivation per mode: found NOT achievable additively under the current primitive shapes; text-only paper assumption plus a small Lean obstruction-witness recommended instead
goal_statement: Assess whether Assumption 2(c)-style honest-slot uniqueness for each rotation mode's EUF-CMA surface (KeyStealingEUFCMA, mode 1; SchedCoreUnforgeable, modes 2-3) can be DERIVED from a timed model plus an honest-only no-back-dating hypothesis, mirroring TimedSig.lean's sigUnforgeableRecent_of_timed, while honoring the owner's standing rejection of NoBackdate/forward-security as a constraint on STOLEN keys (a stolen key signs anything, at any real slot, forever -- memory/key-rotation-mission.md:15-29). Finding: a clean, sound, trust-reducing positive derivation is NOT achievable for any of the three modes without editing an existing assumed structure's type (forbidden by the additive-only constraint) -- the obstruction is structural, not merely a matter of the owner's NoBackdate policy, and survives even granting a maximally permissive honest-custody hypothesis. The two feasible deliverables are (a) an exact-wording text-only paper assumption, scoped to honest non-stolen custody only, and (b) two small, sound, additive Lean theorems that formally witness the obstruction (so the paper's 'not derived' claim is machine-checked, not just asserted), each with a thin Molt/ wrapper so the paper's citations resolve in the paper-aligned library per the repo's own layout convention. Both are designed below in full; no positive derivation is designed, because none exists under the constraints -- this is reported as the honest verdict of the assessment, per (1)-(5) of the work item's own instructions.

new_files.outline: namespace MoltPetit.Model. Imports MoltPetit.Model.KeyStealingSchedule (for badSched) and MoltPetit.Model.KeyStealing (for badKeyrotOn); no import of TimedSig.lean is needed (nothing here touches TimedExecution/NoBackdate/projectSigned -- see 'Derivation sketch' in `recommendation` for why). Module doc (~25 lines) states the obstruction in prose: KeyStealingEUFCMA.unforgeable and SchedCoreUnforgeable.unforgeable are premised on a SINGLE verifying key index `j` not being stolen; TimedExecution's honest-real-slot fields (honest_once, honest_stamp) and TimedSig.NoBackdate built on them are premised on the WHOLE real slot being uncorrupted, which for badSched/badKeyrotOn (the repo's own key-rotation corruption predicates) is an EXISTENTIAL over every key index the schedule/floor admits at that slot -- not just the one that verifies. Two theorems (below) exhibit this gap concretely: a slot where one key is unstolen yet the slot is bad anyway because a DIFFERENT eligible key there is stolen. Then two short theorems (constructive, no Classical needed): `badSched_single_key_safe_not_enough` (mode 2/3 shape) and `badKeyrotOn_single_key_safe_not_enough` (mode 1 shape). Roughly 90-110 lines total including docstrings.

New axiom-guard file (per the constraint: a NEW guard file, not an edit to the existing MoltPetit/Results/Axioms.lean). Imports MoltPetit.Model.KeyStealingTimedScope. Two `#guard_msgs in #print axioms` blocks, one per new theorem, following the exact idiom already used by MoltPetit/Results/Axioms.lean:93-98 for sigUnforgeableRecent_of_timed/noBackdate_independent. Expected result: both theorems are pure constructive existentials over Nat/List/Prop with no Finset-filter-over-Prop step, so they plausibly need NO classical axioms at all (`#print axioms` prints an empty list) -- confirm on build and adjust the `/-- info: ... -/` literal to match rather than assuming `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` by default. ~25-35 lines.

namespace Molt. Imports Molt.Rotation (for the already-existing Molt-namespace `badSched`/`badKeyrot`/`producer`, and their `_eq_core` bridge lemmas) and MoltPetit.Model.KeyStealingTimedScope (for the two core witness theorems). This is the pattern-fix for the finding raised on run 1 of this design: CLAUDE.md's Layout section states the Molt/ lean_lib exists precisely so 'every paper2 Lean citation resolves here', and that is enforced today, not aspirational -- paper/molt.tex:163,780 already cite `badKeyrot_lossOnly`/`badSched_lossOnly` by BARE (unqualified, no `Molt.` prefix -- confirmed zero `\code{Molt.` occurrences anywhere in paper/molt.tex) name, and both are Molt-namespace theorems in Molt/Rotation.lean:230,239 that call directly into the MoltPetit.Model original as their proof term, relying on `badKeyrot_eq_core`/`badSched`-as-abbrev being definitionally equal (Molt/Rotation.lean:182: `badKeyrot_eq_core : badKeyrot = MoltPetit.Model.badKeyrotOn := rfl`; `badSched` itself is `abbrev badSched := @MoltPetit.Model.badSched`, Molt/Rotation.lean:134). Two wrapper theorems here follow the identical idiom: `badSched_single_key_safe_not_enough` (stated over `Molt.badSched`/`Molt.producer`, discharged by directly supplying `MoltPetit.Model.badSched_single_key_safe_not_enough` as the proof term -- typechecks by the same `abbrev`/defeq route `badSched_lossOnly` already uses) and `badKeyrot_single_key_safe_not_enough` (stated over `Molt.badKeyrot`, discharged by `MoltPetit.Model.badKeyrotOn_single_key_safe_not_enough`, typechecking via the same `rfl`-defeq route `badKeyrot_lossOnly` already uses -- confirmed: `Molt.producer n s := s % n` is syntactically identical to `MoltPetit.Model.producerForSlot n slot := slot % n`, bridged by `producer_eq_core := rfl` at Molt/Protocol.lean:112, so both wrapper bodies are one-line `:=` assignments, no `by` tactic block needed). ~20-30 lines including docstrings.

New axiom-guard file for the Molt-namespace wrappers (per the constraint: a NEW guard file, not an edit to the existing Molt/Axioms.lean, mirroring the same additive-guard-file treatment already applied to MoltPetit/Results/AxiomsKeyStealingTimedScope.lean above). Imports Molt.KeyStealingTimedScope. Two `#guard_msgs in #print axioms` blocks for `Molt.badSched_single_key_safe_not_enough` and `Molt.badKeyrot_single_key_safe_not_enough`, following the exact idiom already used throughout Molt/Axioms.lean (e.g. its `badKeyrot_lossOnly`/`badSched_lossOnly` entries). Since the wrapper bodies are literally the core theorems' proof terms under a defeq restatement, the axiom list should match the core theorems' exactly (expected: no classical axioms, same as their MoltPetit.Model originals) -- confirm on build rather than assume. ~15-20 lines.

new_theorems.conclusion: ∃ (n : Nat) (schedule : Nat → Nat) (rented : ByzantineSlots) (Stolen : Nat → Nat → Prop) (s j : Nat), ¬ rented s ∧ ¬ Stolen (producerForSlot n s) j ∧ badSched n schedule rented Stolen s
new_theorems.proof_sketch: Witness n := 1, schedule := fun _ => 0, rented := fun _ => False, Stolen := fun _ j' => j' = 1, s := 0, j := 0. producerForSlot 1 0 = 0. ¬rented 0 is `id`/`not_false`. ¬Stolen(0,0) is `by decide` (0 ≠ 1). badSched 1 (fun _=>0) rented Stolen 0 unfolds (KeyStealingSchedule.lean:124-126) to `False ∨ ∃ j', 0 ≤ j' ∧ Stolen(0,j')`; supply `Or.inr ⟨1, by omega, rfl⟩` since Stolen(0,1) is `1 = 1`. ~15-20 lines incl. docstring.

paper_changes.change: Add, verbatim: '\begin{assumption}[No back-dating, honest custody --- per mode]\label{ass:rotation-honest} Fix a rotation mode and a producer $i$ whose currently active delegate key has been neither rented nor stolen at real slot $r$. B.slot`/`¬ badKeyrotOn(...) B.slot` (the all-key reading) while `SchedCoreUnforgeable`/`KeyStealingEUFCMA`'s own premise only ever supplies the single-key reading, silently strengthening what is assumed beyond what the primitive it claims to derive actually offers.
risks.mitigation: This design's two core witness theorems (plus their Molt/ wrappers) are exactly the formal proof that (b)'s gap is real and unclosable without extra hypotheses; a future session should build them first and cite them before attempting anything more ambitious, and should treat 'derives KeyStealingEUFCMA/SchedCoreUnforgeable from a timed model' as requiring a NEW (not edited) primitive, which is multi-session research explicitly out of scope here (see `alternatives_rejected`).

risks.risk: The exact-wording paper assumption (ass:rotation-honest) is inserted without also updating any theorem statement that currently cites Assumption 2(c) alone, producing an orphaned assumption nothing in the paper's results actually uses.
risks.mitigation: The assumption is presented as documentation of what KeyStealingEUFCMA/SchedCoreUnforgeable already implicitly assume (matching their existing Lean docstrings, e.g. KeyStealingUnique.lean's 'Provenance' paragraph), not as a new formal premise threaded into any theorem's hypothesis list -- no proof anywhere needs to change, and the paper_changes entries say this explicitly ('stated directly rather than derived').

risks.risk: A future session edits MoltPetit.Model.badSched or MoltPetit.Model.badKeyrotOn's definitions (even additively, e.g. by generalizing them) without noticing the two Molt/ wrapper theorems' proofs are bare one-line term assignments that rely on exact defeq (abbrev-transparency for badSched, rfl for badKeyrot via badKeyrot_eq_core) -- if that defeq ever breaks, the wrappers fail to typecheck with no other symptom.
risks.mitigation: This is the same fragility badKeyrot_lossOnly/badSched_lossOnly already carry today (they use the identical one-line-term idiom), so it is an existing, accepted pattern in this codebase, not a new risk introduced by this design; `lake build Molt` fails loudly and immediately if the defeq breaks, well before the guard files' `#guard_msgs` would even be reached.

alternatives_rejected.alt: Reuse sigUnforgeableRecent_of_timed directly, instantiated per mode with `bad := rented` only (ignore key theft in TimedExecution/NoBackdate, fold Stolen only into the abstract Signed predicate/crypto bridge).
alternatives_rejected.why: Unrealizable: TimedExecution n rented log G would assert honest_once/honest_stamp at every real slot that is merely not physically rented, including real slots where the adversary is actively using a stolen key (key_match only constrains the STAMP residue class, not whether the mint is honest) -- exactly the behaviour the mode's own threat model (KeyStealing.lean's module doc: 'a stolen delegate key signs anything, at any slot, forever') requires to be possible. The hypothesis would be false for any real execution with live theft outside rented slots, making the 'derivation' vacuous for the interesting case.

alternatives_rejected.alt: Fold Stolen into bad via the existing badSched/badKeyrotOn (which already combine rent and theft) and route the crypto bridge's premise through ¬bad B.slot, matching TimedExecution's real-slot granularity.
alternatives_rejected.why: Type-mismatched against the primitives being derived: badSched/badKeyrotOn's badness is `rented s ∨ ∃ j' (eligible), Stolen(i,j')` -- an EXISTENTIAL over every key version the schedule/floor admits at s. But `KeyStealingEUFCMA.unforgeable`/`SchedCoreUnforgeable.unforgeable` are premised on `¬ Stolen(i,j)` for the SINGLE verifying j, with no constraint on any other key index. Single-key safety does not entail `¬bad(s)` (a different, unused key at the same slot could be stolen) -- formally witnessed by the two new theorems in this design. The bridge could not be honestly discharged from the structures' own stated premises.

alternatives_rejected.alt: Weaken KeyStealingEUFCMA/SchedCoreUnforgeable's `unforgeable` field to tie the verifying `j` to the block's own declared `keyIndex` (the only `j` any actual caller ever uses, per `rotated_key_dead`/`rotated_key_dead_sched`), which would make the single-key/all-key gap disappear.
alternatives_rejected.why: Forbidden outright: this edits the TYPE of an existing, already-assumed Prop-structure, which the owner's additive-only constraint does not permit regardless of how well-motivated the change is. (It would also be the right fix if the constraint were relaxed -- worth flagging to the owner as an open question, see below.)

alternatives_rejected.alt: Introduce a brand-new, additive, per-(producer,version)-timed EUF-CMA primitive (not editing the old ones) that IS naturally derivable from a versioned timed log, and treat the existing KeyStealingEUFCMA/SchedCoreUnforgeable as a separate, still-primitive surface.
alternatives_rejected.why: Rejected for THIS item's scope, not rejected as an idea: it needs a materially larger new abstraction (a timed log keyed by real slot AND key version, not just real slot; new custody/provisioning hypotheses per mode) and, for mode 1 specifically, both W3a's not-yet-designed real-time/inForce bridge and an undocumented StolenMint <-> Stolen(i,j) bridge that KeyStealing.lean's own module doc flags as unbuilt ('a separate bridge hypothesis in Phase 3'). This is multi-session research-level work, explicitly outside the 'lower priority, keep compact' framing of this work item; recorded here as a candidate future item, not designed further.

alternatives_rejected.alt: Cite the two witness theorems' bare MoltPetit.Model names directly from paper/molt.tex, skipping the Molt/ wrapper entirely, on the grounds that they are a minor negative/obstruction result rather than a headline theorem.
alternatives_rejected.why: Rejected on the adversarial finding against run 1 of this design: CLAUDE.md's Layout section is explicit and, per the maintained precedent (badKeyrot_lossOnly/badSched_lossOnly, already bare-cited from paper/molt.tex:163,780 and living only as Molt-namespace wrappers), enforced in practice -- 'every paper2 Lean citation resolves here [Molt/]'. Nothing about being a minor/negative result exempts a citation from that convention; the fix costs ~20-30 lines of one-line term-mode wrappers under an existing defeq bridge, so there is no material reason to special-case these two theorems out of it.

open_questions_for_owner: Given the finding that the obstruction is structural (single-key vs whole-slot premise mismatch) and survives regardless of the NoBackdate-for-stolen-keys policy, is it worth relaxing the additive-only constraint just for KeyStealingEUFCMA/SchedCoreUnforgeable's `unforgeable` field -- narrowing its `j` to the block's declared `keyIndex` -- the one edit that would actually make a timed-model derivation possible? This would need to go through the normal review path for editing an existing assumed structure, not through this (additive-only) rollout.

Is the small, low-value Lean obstruction-witness (badSched_single_key_safe_not_enough / badKeyrotOn_single_key_safe_not_enough plus their two Molt/ wrappers, ~190 lines total) worth building at all, given its only benefit is upgrading the paper's 'not derived' claim from asserted to machine-checked? It carries essentially zero risk and no dependency, so the main cost is review attention, not engineering effort.

Should Assumption ass:rotation-honest be added to the paper now (this item's primary recommendation) even though nothing currently cited it before, or would the owner rather leave the existing 'assumed, not derived' language in the Named-seams paragraph as sufficient and skip the new assumption environment entirely?
hypothesis_verdict: Directionally right on shape, wrong on feasibility. The three-step shape (bridge / custody / honest-only no-back-dating) is exactly the right decomposition and it generalizes cleanly ACROSS modes via one shared generic engine IF the custody step could be discharged -- but it cannot be, for a reason the hypothesis did not anticipate and that is independent of the owner's already-known NoBackdate-for-stolen-keys rejection: TimedExecution/NoBackdate's 'custody' is a per-REAL-SLOT fact (honest_once/honest_stamp fire once ¬bad(r) is known for the WHOLE slot), while KeyStealingEUFCMA/SchedCoreUnforgeable's 'not stolen' hypothesis is per individual KEY VERSION j. A slot can have one safe key and one stolen key simultaneously (formally witnessed by the two new theorems), so 'this key is safe' cannot be upgraded to 'this slot is safe' without either an unrealizable timed hypothesis (bad := rented only) or silently assuming something stronger than the EUF-CMA surface it is supposed to derive (bad := badSched/badKeyrotOn in the bridge's premise, which the surface's own type does not supply). Net: REFUTED as a cheap, sound, trust-reducing derivation achievable within the additive-only constraint; the shape survives as a correct description of what WOULD work if the existing primitives' per-key premise were narrowed to the declared key index -- which is an edit, not an addition, and therefore off the table here.
recommendation: (1) Minimal timed structure / stolenAt sharing: none needed, and none should be shared with W3a/W5 for this item as designed -- the two obstruction witnesses use only the already-existing, timeless `badSched` (KeyStealingSchedule.lean:124) and `badKeyrotOn` (KeyStealing.lean:47); no new timed structure and no `stolenAt : Nat -> Nat -> Nat -> Prop` shape is introduced or required, because there is no positive derivation for such a structure to feed. (2) Per-mode NoBackdate variant, stated exactly: given the obstruction, the honest content is stated directly as the paper assumption `ass:rotation-honest` (exact LaTeX in `paper_changes`), not as a Lean structure -- 'for a producer whose currently active key is neither rented nor stolen at real slot r, its block (if any) at r is stamped exactly r and declares exactly its currently active key version at r; this says nothing about rented or stolen slots.' changes_made: [major, addressed] Confirmed the finding against the actual sources: paper/molt.tex:163 and :780 cite `badKeyrot_lossOnly`/`badSched_lossOnly` by bare (unqualified) name, and both resolve only as Molt/Rotation.lean:230,239 theorems (guarded in Molt/Axioms.lean), even though the underlying corruption predicates and proofs live in MoltPetit.Model. Also confirmed there are zero `\code{Molt.`-prefixed citations anywhere in paper/molt.tex, i.e. the paper's convention is to cite BARE names that resolve inside the Molt/ namespace, not qualified MoltPetit.Model names. Run 1 of this design broke that convention by proposing to cite `badSched_single_key_safe_not_enough`/`badKeyrotOn_single_key_safe_not_enough` from paper/molt.tex while only defining them in MoltPetit.Model with no Molt/ wrapper. Fixed by adding two new files, `Molt/KeyStealingTimedScope.lean` (two one-line-term wrapper theorems, `badSched_single_key_safe_not_enough` and `badKeyrot_single_key_safe_not_enough` -- the latter renamed to drop 'On', matching how `badKeyrot_lossOnly` already renames `badKeyrotOn_lossOnly` on the way into Molt/) and `Molt/AxiomsKeyStealingTimedScope.lean` (a new guard file, not an edit to the existing Molt/Axioms.lean, mirroring the MoltPetit-side guard file already in the design), plus two new import lines in Molt.lean (the permitted touch class). Verified the wrapper technique is sound and cheap before committing to it: `Molt.badSched` is literally `abbrev badSched := @MoltPetit.Model.badSched` (Molt/Rotation.lean:134) and `Molt.badKeyrot = MoltPetit.Model.badKeyrotOn` by `rfl` (`badKeyrot_eq_core`, Molt/Rotation.lean:182), with `Molt.producer = MoltPetit.Model.producerForSlot` also by `rfl` (`producer_eq_core`, Molt/Protocol.lean:112) -- so both wrappers are one-line term-mode proofs (`:= MoltPetit.Model.<name>`), the identical idiom `badKeyrot_lossOnly`/`badSched_lossOnly` already use, adding roughly 35-45 lines total (two small files + two guard entries + two Molt.lean import lines), consistent with the finding's own '~20-40 extra lines' estimate. Updated paper_changes to cite the corrected bare name `badKeyrot_single_key_safe_not_enough` (not `badKeyrotOn_single_key_safe_not_enough`) in both the new assumption block and the appendix closing sentence, matching the Molt-side rename. Updated size_estimate_lines (150 -> 190), effort_sessions (~0.25 -> ~0.3 session), added a matching alternatives_rejected entry recording why the wrapper is not skippable, and added one new risks entry about the wrapper proofs' defeq-fragility (an existing, accepted pattern in this codebase already carried by badKeyrot_lossOnly/badSched_lossOnly, not a new risk this design introduces).
